newsitem.title: GERMANY: Opel says EU searched two offices last year.
newsitem.headline: Opel says EU searched two offices last year.

text.p: Germany's Adam Opel AG, a unit of U.S. group General Motors, on Friday said the European Commission had searched two of the group's offices in the Netherlands late last year.

In answer to a Reuter query, Opel said, "There have been no searches and there are no searches being conducted at Adam Opel AG. The European Commission however searched through offices at one Dutch Opel dealer and at Opel Niederlande late last year."

Opel responded to questions after EU sources said the Commission had raided offices of German carmakers Mercedes- Benz AG and Opel in connection with alleged irregularities in vehicle pricing and distribution arrangements.
Mercedes-Benz confirmed that some offices had been searched but that the headquarters in Stuttgart had not been visited.
News of the raids emerged as the Commission released details of car price differentials across 12 of the EU's 15 member countries, excluding Greece, Finland and Denmark.
Commission data up until November 1, 1996 showed that 23 of the EU's 75 best-selling models were cheapest in the Netherlands while 21 were cheapest in Portugal.

The Commission said parallel trade in cars, when customers try to buy vehicles elswehere in the EU when price differences make it attractive to do so, was being blocked in Germany, Belgium, Spain and the Netherlands.
